And it was already communicated, the fact that those people were there in those houses, and the police simply came in and picked them up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll proceed after the break. It's already 10 after 10.00, and we will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed, and the cross-examination can proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, before doing that, I have to tell you something. A moment ago, I objected to the fact that Mr. Alic's statement was not disclosed to me, the statement of 2005, and now, during the break, the Prosecution provided me with two statements, two from 2006 and one -- one from 2006 and the other from 2007. And in keeping with Rule 92 bis, confirmation or certificate. Now, I received that, that's true, but here we heard Mr. Alic made a statement in 2005, and that's the one I don't have much all I have is an agreement from Mr. Alic that his previous statements can be used in trials before the International Tribunal or other institutions, as the formulation is here. Anyway, if there was a misunderstanding, the misunderstanding was caused by the Prosecutor. Now I want to ask the following question: Is there a third statement by Mr. Alic before the proofing session that the Prosecution had with him three days ago? If there has, I've still not be disclosed of it. Now, if they call the statement of 2005, provided by the authorised official, I'm asking why they're calling this authorised official's version a statement by Mr. Alic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We're glad that Mr. Seselj has confirmed that he has already obtained these documents. Then is the 92 bis package of 1995 covering 1996 and 1997? There's no ambiguity there. I have a list here of everything that was disclosed, with a disclosure letter. If it's useful, I may distribute it right now, but it corroborates all the -- it corroborates the fact that everything was disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you well, in 2005, the document of 2005 is not a new statement. According to the 92 bis statement, it referred to the statements made in 1996 and 1997. There is no new written statement for July 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, this is in the 92 bis procedure. There is no new statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please, Mr. Seselj, proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is really the case, then I assume everything has been cleared up. But still there is a shadow of doubt, as far as I'm concerned, but I can't do anything else and act upon it. So I'll have to be satisfied with the explanation just given.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Anyway, Mr. Alic, here you state that members of the Serbian Radical Party, and you said that in several places, took part in the conflicts in Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There was no conflict in Zvornik. They launched an attack on Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the side that was attacked, I assume, defended itself. You shot, didn't you, and then you became afraid and fled. Fadil Mujic said that nobody during that attack on your side was killed. Do you know that statement by Fadil Mujic? He was the chief of the crime department.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He probably said that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say that somebody was killed during that conflict?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nobody in the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. But there was a conflict, and I state that the attack was launched by those who had previously taken control of Zvornik, armed the citizens, among them criminals, and that this led to the exodus of the Serb population. You said that the attack was launched by those who entered into the conflict on the 8th of April, so we don't have to agree on that matter. We were on opposite sides, so we can disagree. But you heard that members of the Serbian Radical Party arrived there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As a highly-positioned police official, you know that volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party came to Mali Zvornik from Belgrade; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As a high police official, I assume that you must have known how it was that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party came to Mali Zvornik from Belgrade. Somebody must have reported that, informed you of that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We knew that they were -- that they came there frequently, but that was in Serbia, not Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This came frequently, I really don't know what that means. They came once and they came in two buses. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just on one occasion, that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That was just prior to the conflict; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know how many of them arrived, but I know that there were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you. They came in two busloads, two busloads of them arrived, and you know that Arkan's men came, too; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can claim what I know for certain, and this is what I know: I know that from seeing people who were in the Public Security Station, who had been taken into custody, that's the best proof, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, we haven't come to that yet. Why are you trying to escape from the topic we're discussing? You heard and say in your statement that Arkan's men arrived, and then you said that they held the barricade at Karakaj; isn't that what you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I don't know if Arkan's men were indeed in Karakaj, but I do know that that's where the Serb police in Zvornik had its headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Arkan's men arrived. Do you know how Arkan's men arrived?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know on that on the previous day, the police patrol that went out to Pilica was stopped at the barricade by Arkan's men and was disarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. That means that you don't know that Arkan's men arrived by bus as well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what means of transport they used, but I know they were there. I don't know how many that were there, but I know they arrived in buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you challenging that, when I tell you that they arrived in buses?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and pauses between question and answer for the benefit of one and all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that there was a tank battalion there which held four positions in the area around Zvornik, commanded by Dragan Obrenovic; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The armoured battalion came from Jastrebarsko, withdrawing from Croatia, and went to Celopek.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, you should know that the JNA had engaged a certain number of reservists from the Zvornik area. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, among the reservists -- were the reservists mostly Serbs or almost exclusively Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that because the Muslims refused to respond to the JNA call-up to become included in the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it also true and correct that the Muslim authorities from Sarajevo, and personally present, Alija Izetbegovic, called upon the Muslims not to respond to the call-up for mobilisation of the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct, because the Muslims were sent to battle fronts in Croatia, so that was the reason they were told not to respond to that call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That might have been the reason. I'm not interested in the reasons, I'm not going to go into that. I'm just interested in facts. So we agree there about the facts. So the Muslims were set aside through their own free will. They were called up to join the reserve force, and the structure would have been the same as the national composition was, had they responded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the interpreters are begging you once again to speak slower to make breaks. You know, they're doing excellent work. Sometimes they manage to translate in realtime, but sometimes, you know, they have a very hard time trying to follow you because you're going so fast. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'll slow down, I'll promise to slow down, but I don't know how long I'll be able to keep my promise, because very often to be quite frank I forget my promises. And since Mr. Alic and I understand each other very well, although we're on opposite sides, that's what happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, had all the Muslims responded to the call-up to go to the reserve force of the JNA, would that mean that the structure of those units, those JNA units, would have been identical to the structure of the population of Zvornik Municipality, so almost 50/50, a little more Muslims perhaps than Serbs, but roughly 50/50?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that wouldn't have meant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because the Muslims in that war were just being used, and ultimately what happened to us in Bosnia-Herzegovina happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, these are all assumptions and speculation, what would have happened if this happened. Anyway, what would have happened, Mr. Alic, had the Muslim authorities from Sarajevo proclaimed the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Would there have been war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because your aspirations and those for a Greater Serbia would have meant a new Yugoslavia and Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, no part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But leave aside my aspirations, Mr. Alic. I was an individual at the head of a very small party and the only deputy in Parliament. Do you know about the Belgrade Declaration?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that an agreement was reached with the -- between the authorities in Belgrade and Izetbegovic, personally, that Bosnia-Herzegovina should remain within the composition of a rump Yugoslavia and that Izetbegovic should be the first president of such a Yugoslavia? Do you know about that, do you know of that agreement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not. That was politics. I don't enter into politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. If you don't, I'm not going to force you to state your views in the matter. Now, on several occasions here, you mentioned Dragan Spasojevic, and he was the commander of the police in Zvornik, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were his deputy; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that Dragan Spasojevic took part in a crime against the Muslims, any civilians, soldiers, policemen, whatever; Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, your relationship with Dragan Spasojevic, were they correct and proper?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very correct and professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you had a good opinion of him, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Now, Dragan Spasojevic says hello to you, and sent me his statement, in which he says things about those same events -- he talks about the same events that you talked about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj's first comment is totally inappropriate as to what Mr. Dragan Spasojevic can say to the witness. As for the rest, he may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand that objection from the Prosecutor. What could Dragan Spasojevic say to the witness? I have Dragan Spasojevic's statement here before me, and I want to show it to the witness. Could it be placed on the overhead projector? I've tried to ensure photocopying of this document. However, the photocopy machine was otherwise engaged, so that was not possible. It was working elsewhere. Have you already copied it? Have you handed it 'round. If you have, that's very good. It is 1/1. Great, so it is successful. I thought we were going to have problems with the photocopying procedure. Anyway, let's put this on the overhead projector, it is Dragan Spasojevic's statement, so we can see what he says here. He says that he knows you personally, he knows that you worked in Belgrade, that you went to Zvornik, and then what we're interested in is his statements about what you did in Zvornik. Is that on our screens, is it on the overhead? Right. Anyway, Dragan Spasojevic says of you the following: "In Zvornik, he worked to rally the active and reserve police force of Muslim ethnicity and prepared the formation of a Muslim MUP. He effected close cooperation with a man named Hajra who was sent from the SDA leadership to four Muslim territorial units and to train the military and arm them." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you yourself said that in the police station, on two occasions meetings were held of the Crisis Staff, the crisis staff of a political party, the Party of Democratic Action, which rallied Muslims, and that you attended those meetings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine. And then Spasojevic goes on to state the following: "Asim Alic became actively included in infiltrating members of the paramilitary units of the Patriotic League into the reserve force of the police of the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and thereby through regular channels armed the units of the Patriotic League." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who, then, Mr. Alic, just prior to the conflict, distributed a full set of weapons from the police station in Zvornik to the Muslim population, then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The populous broke through into the de-person warehouse and picked up the weapons themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And armed themselves well?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there wasn't much weapons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, several hundred automatic rifles were there, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That piece of information is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, then. How many automatic rifles were there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before that, the entire reserve force of the police was called up, and they were 50 per cent Serbs, 50 per cent Muslims at the time, and they were armed with those weapons and they were our reserve policemen, our reserve force, because in our warehouses there might have been just a certain number of weapons which were issued to the active police force and also to the reserve police force. They had no other reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And as you said, the people broke through into the warehouses, and how many rifles did they come across there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Very few.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see, very few weapons, very few rifles. Anyway, Spasojevic goes on to say about you that in October 1991, he or you took part in the formation of the first units of the Patriotic League in the village of Godus where to this day there is a monument as a remembrance of that event. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is not true at all. In October, I moved to Zvornik to work, and here it says "seven months ago."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here it says "in October 1991." That's the fifth paragraph on page 1.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I moved from Belgrade to Zvornik only in October to work, so I didn't know the people, I didn't know the place. How was I then supposed to organise all that? That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say here that you organised it. It says here that you participated in the forming.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's not true, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And is there a monument commemorating this event?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, at the entrance to the village of Godus, there is a plaque where it says that the villagers of the village of Godus were the first to offer resistance to the aggressor, so it is not a monument.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when did they offer resistance?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I know that there were some skirmishes up at Majevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What kind of skirmishes and gunfire in Majevica, Mr. Alic, please? Come on. Before the conflict in Zvornik, there was nothing up there.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, then you know more about it than I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, yes, because I studied that, and you were not prepped for your testimony properly.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, this paragraph that you tried to misinterpret does not refer to you. It says here: "Seven months before the conflict broke out, they set up a unit of the Patriotic League with about 150 members, with full infantry equipment, clothes, helmets, flak-jackets, automatic weapons. This event engendered a response on the Serbian side. The Serbs started arming themselves because of the bad experience from the Second World War with the Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No? Fair enough. Is it true that when Cutileiro's plan was passed in March 1992, Momcilo Mandic sent an official dispatch calling for the MUP employees in Zvornik to state their affiliation, which side they wanted to be on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's not how it was worded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How was it worded, then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We'd received a dispatch from the Federal Secretariat of the Interior that we should go to our rally in Sarajevo to express our commitment to have unified police, to lend our support to the unified police force in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And only the Muslim police officers went there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's a different matter. Are you aware of Momcilo Mandic's dispatch?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know about Momcilo Mandic's dispatch. It says in there that all the valuables that were seized and that were in the Public Security Station should be handed over to the federal SUP, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're not aware of the other thing?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you attend a collegium meeting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you talk about the separation or the division of the MUP in terms of personnel and equipment?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there was no such agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, Dragan Spasojevic says there was such an agreement and that you attended this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Dragan Spasojevic can say whatever he wants to. I am saying what I'm saying, and that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, what Dragan Spasojevic is claiming is also true.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, it is impossible to interpret at this rate of speed. The speakers are kindly asked to slow down and make questions [as interpreted] before questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, again I'm sorry that we have to ask you, both of you, to slow down. Mr. Witness, if you could look at the cursor on the screen in front of you, then you will notice that it stops running when the interpretation has ended. That might be another indication for you as to when you can reply to questions put to you by the accused. So please be aware of the movements on the screen in front of you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, let us move on to the next claim made by Mr. Spasojevic. He says: "Asim Alic, that evening, together with the criminals from Zvornik and members of the Patriotic League, organised and led an action to take the Public Security Station in Zvornik, where a bloodbath was avoided by pure chance. This incident caused a definitive split in the Zvornik police and of course in the people, among the people too. That's when the Serb police officers withdrew to Karakaj, where there was a majority Serb population." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what you said, that the people spontaneously broke into the depots, that was not really spontaneous. You lead the people, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why should Dragan Spasojevic be lying?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, what am I supposed to be saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you say what you're supposed to say. That doesn't matter, because the Prosecution trusts Dragan Spasojevic more than it trusts you. And then he says: "Alic personally led the group that broke into the depots of the Public Security Station in Zvornik and seized weapons, uniforms, official IDs and other equipment of the Minister of the Interior, distributing all of that to members of the Patriotic League and local criminals." Listing them, Behulj [phoen], Musadic [phoen], Kalilovic [phoen] and others: "This forced all the Serbs to leave Zvornik, and Asim Alic, with the group that he led, broke into apartments and houses of eminent Serbs - names are listed here, Petko Panic [phoen], Miko Milovanovic [phoen], and Marinko Vasilic [phoen] - and looted those properties. Hardened criminals were stationed at the border crossings with Serbia to prevent Muslims who wanted to cross over into Serbia, because they were aware of the bad situation that Alic and his people created in the city." Is that true, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's not true. That's a notorious lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know Petko Panic, Miko Milovanovic and Marinko Vasilic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Petko Panic was a police officer that was my subordinate, and Miko Milovanovic was a colleague of mine, and he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Mr. Dutertre is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, let us look at the last paragraph of Dragan Spasojevic's statement at page 1. It says: "I know that Alic was tasked by AID to mention that among the captured Serbs, there were members of the Serbian Radical Party. Some people who participated in the arrest talked about that. I also know for sure that he has been in Sarajevo recently, for seven or eight days, to hold some talks at AID." Is that correct, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your examination-in-chief here, you said that you immediately sent a dispatch to Sarajevo and to Tuzla about the fact that four Serbs, wearing uniforms, fully armed, had been arrested. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before moving on to the four whom you arrested, it is mentioned that you went to Sarajevo and there you met the State Security Services or Intelligence Services, and at their request you said that Mr. Seselj could be involved in one way or another. So let me remind you that you have taken the oath and that you have said that you will tell all the truth. If ever we discover that there was a meeting in Sarajevo and that you tell us the opposite, well, then you will be charged with contempt of court. So what do you have to say to these statements made by the witness, who says, "I know that Mr. Alic met AID"? Is it true or is this not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not true at all. I never met with any AID officials, and I don't know where their headquarters is in Sarajevo at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A little while ago, the AID changed its name, did it not, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that there was some talk about that, but I don't know the exact name, because it is an organizational unit that has nothing to do with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it maybe SIPA, S-I-P-A, or close?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it is not SIPA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, at page 2, Dragan Spasojevic describes the way in which the four people were freed. He describes the role of Fadil Mujic, and you confirm that Fadil Mujic had assisted in obtaining their release; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me just read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in return, Fadil Mujic was allowed to leave Zvornik through Serbia and go to Germany; is that right? Just to go through briefly through all these passages so I don't have to read all that. Is it true that Fadil Mujic released the four and was allowed in return to go to Germany via Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's what Fadil told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's not dwell on this for a long time, because I will have the opportunity to discuss this with other people. Now, let me move to the third passage, because it concerns you. Spasojevic says: "When the war began, Asim Alic fled to Tuzla, and on the 22nd of May, 1992, he went from Tuzla to Sapna and was appointed the commander of the Public Security Station. A terrible crime against Serbs and the ethnic cleansing of Serbs happened in Sapna at that time. He personally led the police in the effort to ethnically cleanse and kill the Serb civilians in the villages of Rizanj, Zavid, Rastosnica, and Laze, et cetera. While he was the commander in Sapna, all the Serbs were either killed or expelled, and it became a 100 per cent ethnically pure Muslim territory." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that all the Serbs in Sapna disappeared?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, there was no Serbs in Sapna. Sapna was a ethnically-pure Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How can you say that in Rizanj, Zavid, Rastosnica, and Laze, there were no Serbs? These are all villages around Sapna; is that so? Sapna is now a municipality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And all those villages are in the municipality of Sapna?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where are the Serbs from those villages, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And how many of them were killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't have the figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And as the commander of the Public Security Station in Sapna, did you ever file any criminal reports against any Muslim soldiers, paramilitaries, police officers, armed civilians, for crimes against Serbs; murder, beatings, looting of property, burning of houses?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it was not in my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In whose jurisdiction was that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Military security.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, that's if somebody from the regular army commits a crime. If a civilian commits a crime, an armed civilian, under whose jurisdiction were such crimes?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Under our jurisdiction, but there were no such crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But who burned all those Serb houses in those villages?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you can't, you can't. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we find out, because this is something I did not know, you commanded the police in Sapna, and this something I didn't know about, either; seemingly, some Serbs were killed. As a police commander of the civilian police, you should have carried out investigations. If the investigations established that the perpetrators of the crimes are policemen or belonging to the military, then you are quite right, it is for the military police and the military prosecutor to carry out the investigation and do what is necessary. But if it so happens that among those people who perpetrated these acts, some people were civilians, then it was for you to do something about it. Your answer is elliptical. If you can tell us, as a commander of the police forces, of the civilian police in Sapna, whether you carried out any investigations after some people disappeared or some people were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There weren't any such cases. What is stated here is not the truth. Sapna is an exclusively Muslim place, inhabited by Muslims. Now, the places that Mr. Seselj mentions, there were Serbs there, but in the military operations they were cleansed, in military operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Alic. Dragan Spasojevic goes on to say: "In the course of 1993," and he's referring to you, "Because of his merits, he was appointed chief of the police in Sapna." So that's a higher post and command? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Near his office, for days, there was the head of a Serb, Cedo Nikolic, impaled on a pole, whom the Muslims had taken prisoner, had captured in a purely Serb village of Boskovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's a notorious lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Had you heard of Cedo Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, but such things never happened in those areas. That's ludicrous.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you don't assume that Dragan Spasojevic is lying, these are total lies, or why would a colleague of yours lie when you say you're on good terms?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking that myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He goes on to say about you: "He left Sapna because of crimes and the trafficking -- illegal trafficking of cigarettes, and through his criminal associates, he was placed commander of the Tuzla Canton MUP units, and that unit was well known because of its special brutality in the ethnic cleansing of Vozuca and the surrounding Serb villages." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is a notorious lie, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that your unit took part in the -- in taking control of Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I know those areas better than you, and that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You didn't take part in taking control of Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My unit was in Vozuca to protect the material property there, because the army had already freed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And where are the Serb civilians from Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They left together with the army, when the army withdrew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, why did they leave?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Ask the 2nd Corps that, who liberated the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And who is the commander of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How do you not know who the commander of the 2nd Corps was of your army, how could you not know that? How should I know if you don't?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I see you know everything, so you should know that, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're the witness here, not me. When I am a witness, I'll say what I know, but now you must tell me who the commander of the 2nd Corps was.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember the name. There were three of them. Zeljko Knez was there first, then there was Azim Sadic, and after that there was -- there was another commander. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine. If you happen to remember, tell us.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After the war, he issued false documents in the name of those who had died, were killed, or Muslims living abroad, so that in that way he could populate places in the Republika Srpska with Muslims, and then these names are mentioned, Mahala Jusici, Dugi Do; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They're all Muslim places that you are mentioning now, and this is one of a series of lies that he is putting forward. And I'd like to see that letter if possible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Of course, this will all be published in the newspaper in a few days, but he says they aren't Muslims places -- Mahala Jusici and Dugi Do are Muslim places, but what he says is this: That the Muslims who lived there, that they had either died, been killed, or left and took up residence abroad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry for interrupting, but I would like to seek certification of the decision you handed down a few moments ago as regards a document quoted by Mr. Seselj and the protective measures therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you are saying this in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I haven't quoted any names, but we can move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall move into private session, and in the meantime, before redaction is ordered, so, please, Mr. Registrar, please issue an order for this to be redacted, and the Trial Chamber will deliberate instantly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber, after having deliberated on the matter, has rejected the request for certification in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a second issue which is not connected to the first one. The documents which Mr. Seselj relies on during his cross-examination were given to me when the cross-examination had started already. I believe that this is a problem, and the OTP can legitimately expect these documents to be provided to him before the beginning of the cross-examination. I would like a decision to be taken on the matter, which I think it's an issue relating to the equality of arms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, this document which you had received, according to the fax number we can read on the document, this seems to indicate that you received it on the 15th of May, at 13 minutes past 2.00. No, the 14th of May. How is it that you did not disclose this at the start of the hearing to the Prosecution, since you have mentioned this document in the middle of your cross-examination? I remember that you had asked to have a copy, you wanted to make copies and the photocopying machine wasn't working properly. How can you explain this? The document reached you on the 14th of May and was not disclosed in B/C/S to the Prosecutor this morning before the commencement of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I really did receive the document on the 14th of May, during the examination-in-chief, somewhere towards the end of the in-chief. So I had to read it first, this document and other documents which I received. Then I had to make a selection, and then on Friday -- or, rather, on Thursday and Friday -- or, rather, on Friday and Saturday, I had from 9.00 until 1.00 a visit by high-ranking officials of the Serbian Radical Party, Tomislav Nikolic and Dragan Todorovic, and I assume you're aware of the fact that we're forming a new government in Serbia, and the party whose president I still am is taking part in the formation of that government, so we had to hold consultations about that, and I'm still the party President, although I'm a prisoner here of the enemies of the Serbs. And in the afternoon, my wife visited me. On Thursday -- or, rather, Friday, Saturday, in the afternoon, Sunday morning, and all day Monday. So quite literally, I didn't have any time to take any steps with respect to photocopying, and today, as soon as I arrived here, Mr. Ram came from the Registry, and I gave him those documents over to him to have them copied, and I was afraid they would not be copied because the photocopying machine was engaged. So what else could I do? You know that the prison authorities don't wish to provide me with any photocopying facilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your explanations are satisfactory. You told us and you explained why you were not able, in did due time, to disclose these documents. However, I would have to tell you that I disagree on part of what you said. When I agree with you, I tell you, but when I disagree, I also tell you. You said, "I'm here as a prisoner of those who are against the Serbs." Well, I can tell you that you're not my prisoner, as far as I'm concerned. And as far as the Bench is concerned, we are not anti-Serb, as you seem to say or hint. I wanted this to be said so that everything is clear. Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't really know how difficult this is materially, but I did -- I only obtained these documents during the break, and the cross-examination hardly started. I spent quite a while during the examination-in-chief, and I believe that this time could have been used to make the photocopies so that I could get the documents before the cross-examination started. I don't know when exactly Mr. Seselj gave these documents, but if he had handed them over to the Registry in due time, we could have had the photocopies before the cross-examination started, and I think practically it would be good if things were run that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a problem with this objection. Through this objection, we would not want too much importance to be given to this document. Let me repeat what I have said on many occasions. This document is a statement made by a witness. We don't know how it was made. We don't know much. We only know what is written in this document, but it doesn't prove that things happened that way. The only thing that is certified is the signature of the person making the statement. Mr. Seselj is using this document to ask questions. He was allowed to do this. He is allowed to do this, but I want things to be very clear. This -- according to me, this document should not be given too much importance. The only thing we provide importance to is the answers given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I fully agree with this, I support this, but I would like to make sure that in the future, we have the documents in time. And I don't want to focus on this document, but we should have the document in time so that the OTP can get ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, I fully support what my fellow Judge just said. Of course you may ask a question using a document, but as to the probative value, remember that we have a witness that is under oath. He is challenging what is in the statement. When your own witness comes to testify, he will also be under oath. He will also answer your questions. I'm sure you will use this document to ask your questions. And then the probative value of the document might possibly be at the same level as what the witness is saying today. This is the way things work, and you know it as well as I do. So my fellow Judge was absolutely right to point this out. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, had I not had the assistance of persons who were direct participants in these historical events, I would have absolutely no idea about them. What would I know about Mr. Alic had Dragan Spasojevic not come to my assistance and written what he knows about him? So I can't just invent questions for Mr. Alic. And during the examination-in-chief, I drew your attention to the contradictions in his various statements, and the Prosecutor did his best to hide them. But I wasn't there, I have no idea what happened, and I would never have learned what had happened over there if I had not been accused here of something I did not take part in. Now that I have information, I have sources of where I got the information, so this is proof that I'm not inventing things, since you assumed on many occasions that perhaps I might be inventing things along the way. And let me tell you one more thing. When I said that I was a prisoner here of Serb enemies, the enemies of Serbs, well, I didn't think of you, personally, or your colleagues. True Frenchmen cannot be an enemy of the Serbs, but we have French regimes from Mitterrand onwards who are expressly anti-Serb. But I do believe that many Frenchmen, most Frenchmen are the friends of Serbs from World War I, I know that the Italians were friends of ours, and we've never had any conflicts with the Danes, perhaps because we're very far away from them, that might be one reason; but there was never any hostility or enemy feelings. Now that your regime is against the Serb people, I assume they might be punished as they were -- the Italians were, so I hope that I will see the day arrive when friends of the Serbs in France will come to power. This man Sarkozy is even worse than his predecessors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a political speech, Mr. Seselj, and you're not entitled to do this. You cannot use this as a forum to make political speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what we're interested in is what happened at the time. The rest of what you're saying might be interesting, but please say it in another forum. So please proceed with your cross-examination, and maybe -- just ask the questions that are interesting for your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's round off this question of Dragan Spasojevic. He says one more thing of you. He says: "I know that at the moment he's working in the MUP of the Tuzla Canton and that he was suspended for criminal acts." That is to say, receiving bribes and issuing false documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. I like these short answers. You say it's not correct, he says it is, and we're finished with that. Now, I have another document here. I don't know whether it's been photocopied, whether we had time for that. It's from the Centre for Research of Crime committed on the Serb people," signed by the leader of the center Milivoj Ivanisevic. Have you heard of Milivoj Ivanisevic, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I have not heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Milivoj Ivanisevic intensively and systematically is doing research into crimes against the Serbian population in Bosnia-Herzegovina. You know there war crimes against the Muslims, crimes against the Serbs and crimes against the Croats, and this is indisputable. But he deals with one segment, one section of those crimes, crimes perpetrated against the Serbs in this case. And in that centre of his, your name is mentioned, so I'm going to show a document now and we're going to comment on it briefly which relates to you. Could you just show the first page? We're not going to dwell on it, and move on to page 2 straight away. But let's have it on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Unless I'm wrong, this document was not disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, yes, which document is it? Your documents have numbers "I1" and "2/3." Could you tell us exactly which document you're using?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just place page 1 on the overhead projector. I know it's page 2, but I'm not quite sure. What number is it, number 2? Perhaps we didn't have time to photocopy that. You can see the title page of the document, though. Perhaps we can leave this document until after the break and I could start off with the documents that you do have in your possession. So shall we leave this for the next session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You can address these issues after the break. The document will first be photocopied, because no one has it. Then the Prosecutor will have a copy, as well as the Bench, and you will ask questions on this document after the break. So please move on to another document for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, let's now come to these four people, deal with these four people who were stopped at the Muslim barricade towards Karakaj in the night between the 7th and 8th of April. In your statements, you say that two of those men had membership cards of the Serbian Chetnik Movement and the other two of the Serbian Volunteer Guard; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that two men had membership cards of the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and parallel to that, membership cards of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is not contained in your 1996 and 1997 statements, and that's what I'm referring to. Can you now describe to the Judges here what the membership card of the Serbian Chetnik Movement looked like, or identification card? What did it look like? How do you remember it as being?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The membership card of the Serbian Chetnik Movement was a membership card which, on the first page, had three letters in the Cyrillic, "SCP," which was abbreviated for the Serbian Chetnik Movement, and that was in some sort of circle over which was the Serbian "Tricolor" flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How many pages did the membership card of the Serbian Chetnik Movement have?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You would open it like you would the former ID cards. It was a little bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And how many colours were there on it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, the Prosecution showed you what the Serbian Chetnik Movement ID card looked like. I think it was during the evidence of Protected Witness 007 or the witness before that one, and you were able to see that the Serbian Chetnik Movement ID card is one small card. It doesn't have any pages, and it is only one colour. There is no tri-colour. It is a dark blue item. This was shown to you here, and it was admitted into evidence. I don't recall the actual exhibit number, but I think that you all remember what the Serbian Chetnik Movement card looked like. I think that the Protected Witness 007 talked about that. I'm trying to show you now that this witness doesn't even know what this ID card looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, since you said, about the other two men, that they had ID cards from the Serbian Volunteer Guard, an organisation run by Arkan, you mentioned that Ulemek had an ID card from the French Foreign Legion sewn into somewhere; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So since you were able to find this ID card, which was so well hidden from the French Foreign Legion, did it not occur to you that this man was sent there on some secret task by the French Foreign Legion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because he had other ID cards, including that of Arkan's Tigers and the JNA, and out of those three ID cards I could think that anyone might have sent him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if he was such a collector, don't you find it strange that he didn't have one from the Serbian Chetnik Movement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it didn't surprise me, but, at any rate, he didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So let us now make this clear. If the volunteers from the Serbian Radical Party had arrived by bus the day earlier and if Arkan's men also came by bus a day or two earlier, how come that now we have four men here, two from Arkan's men and two Radicals, in a single car and they get lost? What do you think about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The conversation was so fast that when we want to raise an objection, it's too late. The witness said, if I remember well, that he didn't know whether the volunteers came by bus or not. In the question, there's an assumption. We're asking the -- the witness is asked to speculate. Of course, my objection has lost its meaning, since we had an answer since then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have already heard a good number of volunteers who came here, and we've understood that they arrived by bus, they were transported by bus. So if these individuals are volunteers, why is it that they did not come as a unit, but they came as a force, I mean, in a private car, in a passenger car? It's quite interesting. Can you tell us whether you have any idea why this happened? You may not, especially since when you interviewed these four individuals, you were supposed to know that there are Serbian volunteers that may be coming from Serbia, and you may be aware, notably as a policeman, that these volunteers come in convoys and not individually. So why did you not ask the foursome about this, you know, to ask them who they were, exactly, and what they were doing, especially if one has a card from the French Foreign Legion? You might really wonder why he's there and ask him. As far as I'm concerned, your answers are not quite satisfactory regarding a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I explained this in my statement, and I maintain what I said. Mr. Ulemek had three ID cards; the regular JNA ID card, an ID card issued by the French Foreign Legion, and an ID card --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the last ID card.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I saw the military ID card, I thought he was really a member of the military police, and I wanted to call the army and hand him over to them. But I talked to them on several occasions throughout the day, and I kept gleaning new bits of information. I don't know how they were coming in, but these four came in, in a passenger vehicle, and that passenger vehicle had been seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is Mr. Alic, you mentioned several times, when those four men were arrested, that there was a lot of telephone calls asking for their release; that people intervened from high up, making those phone calls. Can you recall who made those phone calls and who asked for their release? Was it somebody from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer that, because my colleague took all those calls.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that your colleague, Fadil Mujic, who actually had those calls, stated at the trial in Belgrade - I have the transcript of his evidence in its entirety, and so does the Prosecution - that Colonel Boskovic, the head of the Security Service in the JNA at the time, called, and he was promoted to lieutenant general quite soon afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fadil Mujic didn't tell you that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution has Fadil Mujic's statement and can make use of it. When you left Zvornik, you described the circumstances, in part. Apart from this function in the Sapna police station, did you hold any other functions, such as, for instance, any political functions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you a member of the War Presidency in the Zvornik Municipality set up in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it's a political function, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but that was ex officio because of my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please, a member of a War Presidency in a municipality is a political function, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The chief of the Public Security Station, ex officio, is a member of this Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Under which law?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, under the law of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The chief of the police from Sapna is the member -- is a member of the War Presidency of the Municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that's because the police station was relocated to the free territory in the Zvornik Municipality, and the Zvornik Municipality itself had its War Presidency in the free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you were the chief of the police for the entire Municipality of Zvornik, not only for Sapna?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm saying that the chief of the police of the free part of the Zvornik Municipality territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The free territory, that means the territory that you held in your hands, not free for Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you were the chief of the police for the part of Zvornik Municipality under the Muslim control, and you were responsible for everything that was going on in that part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So who, apart from you, was also responsible, as the police chief?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was the police chief, and the civilian situations were within my purview. On the other hand, there was also the military, and since everybody there was in the military, I had very little work to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Since you failed to mention this political function that you held, I have an excerpt from Mirzad Handzic's [phoen] book, entitled "Zvornik from the elections to the Dayton," where your role is confirmed. But since you now confirm that you held this role, there's no need for me to exhibit that. Is it so?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I didn't read this book and I have no reason to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it is my role to read books. A police officer is not expected to read books. He's supposed to wield his truncheon, is he not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you have time enough on your hands to read books.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The four men who were arrested, were they beaten in the course of their arrest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, avoid these comments. It's a waste of time. The only question is whether he had a political office or not. You're saying, "No, you have the opposite proof" because it seems that it's some kind of book called : "After Dayton ... " I don't know exactly what it's called because it's was not recorded on the transcript, author Mizrad Hamdzic seemed to mention the role played by this witness. This is the interesting part, and only this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness recalled later that he did hold this political function, so I wouldn't dwell on that. The point is that this was a major political function that covered the whole territory of the Zemun Municipality that was under the Muslim control after the 1992 conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Zemun is far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Zvornik, not Zemun. Zvornik is close. So I wouldn't really dwell on that and waste any time, it's just a detail, not particularly important, but perhaps of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The four men, were they beaten when they were arrested, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not mistreated or beaten at the Public Security Station, but for sure they were at the roadblock.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were beaten there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I suppose so, because that's what they told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where were they taken from, from the roadblock, first?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the Public Security Station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Not to the firefighters' place and then to the Public Security Station?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fine, we'll deal with that later. Do you know that Dusan Vuckovic, a.k.a., Repic, that he showed up at the places where the Zvornik Muslim were detained, when he killed people and where he tortured people, cut off their ears, when he had his way with them in a really atrocious manner, that he was looking for men called "Boban" and "Zuna," some people by that name?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was told that but I was not able to identify who Boban and Zuna, were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When he was beaten in the course of his arrest, did you learn that Boban and Zuna had beat him up the most brutally, and he learned their names?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's what he told me during the interview at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he told you that immediately. Do you know in 1993, he was put on trial together with his brother, Vojin Vuckovic, at the district court in Sabac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that there is a final judgement sentencing Dusan Vuckovic, a.k.a., Repic, to 20 years in prison for the murder of seven Muslims, because it was not known at that time about the others; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that his brother, Vojin Vuckovic, a.k.a., Zuco, was charged only with false representation and illegal carrying of weapons, and that he was convicted only for the latter; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So no criminal offence could be proven during that trial against him. Do you know that Dusko Vuckovic, a.k.a., Repic, was subjected to psychiatric observation on several occasions following his arrest and during the trial in Sabac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I have a series of documents here confirming that various psychiatrists determined that he was a psychopath. Do you have any reasons to doubt that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I raise an objection. The witness is not a psychiatrist, a psychologist, and cannot have an informed view on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, the witness has interviewed Dusan in the premises of the civilian police of Zvornik. Maybe he noted that he was a psychopath or not. You don't really need to be an expert in psychiatry to know whether a person has psychiatric disorders. It could be interesting, but I will ask the witness myself this question. Witness, according to the documents held by Mr. Seselj, it seems that expert say Dusan Vuckovic was a psychopath. When you saw him, what was he like? Did you think that he had a mental disorder? Did he look like that? What did you think of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't able to notice that he suffered from a mental disorder or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it obvious to you, Mr. Alic, that after all the beatings that he received and in the beatings Zuna and Boban were prominent, that this psychopathy of his went to such brutal limits as a result of that? Now, you're a policeman and you know from your own practice when somebody is subjected to something like that, something clicks in his brain and then he's ready to do something which he would never have thought of in normal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness said that he noticed no mental disorder, and there was a follow-up question to this. I don't wish to repeat what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Dutertre is quite right on this point. When Dusan, Ulemek and the other two people were with you, did you beat them up, all four of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They weren't beaten during the period which they spent at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the police premises, the practice is never to resort to physical force, and that's prescribed by law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness and I agree on one point, that the beating took place before they entered the police station, so there's no dispute about that. They had been beaten, and the witness confirmed that Repic had mentioned Zuno and Boban as the people who had beaten him up. So that's not being disputed. And the witness also said that he doesn't know who Boban and Zuno were, and these were two men who were quite obviously were among the Muslims who had beaten up the other four men. And what happened there was -- or, rather, I tried to elicit an answer from the witness, as a policeman with many years of experience, whether he was able to conclude that what happened was that somebody who looked quite normal and appeared to be normal to him, about these terrible beatings that he was subjected to, became a bloodthirsty criminal, whether he, as a policeman, could arrive at a conclusion like that. So if that isn't a proper question, I'll give up on it and move on. I'm not insisting upon it, but it's quite obvious to me, and that's why I wanted to ask the witness, who is a policeman. He's a witness of justice here, so he could state his views in the matter on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you answer the question or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't answer that question, I just can't. I'm not a professional in the area. Everything would be pure speculation on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that when the new indictment was raised against Dusan Vuckovic, nicknamed Repic, together with Brano Grujic, Branko Pavlovic, and then those people who had nicknames Zoks, Major Toro, Lopov, and Bosanac; and I can't remember all their names, and I seem to remember the nicknames better, but, anyway, he was indicted together with them. I assume you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know things like that. I don't want to talk about them, because I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just remember. You were questioned in Tuzla or Sarajevo with respect to the Belgrade trial?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, but they didn't mention the people you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, their names were mentioned there. I'm going to tell you their real names now. I thought that you might have remembered the nicknames. I have the indictment raised against them here, so I'll read them out. Branko Grujic and Popovic, Branko. You know them, don't you? Then there was Dusko Vuckovic, that's this man Repic; Dragan Slavkovic, his nickname was Major Toro, and you testified in the Dragan Slavkovic trial about that, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you did testify in Belgrade about these people. Don't you know who you testified about?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I testified in the Brano Grujic trial and the Ulemek trial. Now, the people you just mentioned are people I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You did not testify in the Ulemek trial. Mr. Alic, collect your thoughts for a moment. And in what circumstances did you testify in the Ulemek trial?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The group of those four men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ulemek was never tried for Zvornik. I can guarantee you that.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I say that in my statement. Now, whether he was taken to trial or not, I'm not -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I have to remind you of the trial you testified in Belgrade. It was the Branko Grujic, Branko Popovic, aka, Marco Pavlovic, Dusko Vukovic, nicknamed Repic; Dragan Slavkovic, known as Toro or Major Toro; Ivan Korac, whose nicknamed Zoks; Sinica Filipovic [phoen], nicknamed Lopov; and Dragutin Dragicevic, nicknamed Bosanac. Those were the trials in which you testified, and the Prosecutor can confirm that if you don't remember, if you don't know.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is true, but I confirmed the case of the people that I knew personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Alic. Right now, we've established that you were previously questioned in Sarajevo by the investigating judge in Sarajevo pursuant to instructions from Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you were questioned during the investigation, Dusko Vuckovic, nicknamed Repic, was still alive, and later on he committed suicide, he hanged himself in prison. So when you came to testify in Belgrade, you no longer saw him; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard that he had hanged himself in the central prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you almost recognised somebody else as being Repic; wasn't that how it was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, never mind. It's not an essential point. But, anyway, I have here the indictment against these people and, Mr. President, you asked for that and the Prosecution disclosed it to me. I don't know whether they provided it to you. 04615792 is the page I would like to have called up now. 04 -- I'll repeat the page number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have asked to have the indictment. From what I understood, the indictment is being translated, but we still don't have it and we're still waiting for it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, from that lengthy indictment, I'd just like to read out a brief excerpt from page 18, and you can see that on the overhead projector, perhaps: "If the Secretariat provides us with 04615792," that's the page number. You don't have it on e-court. All right, take my copy, and we can just take a look at that part of the indictment, and that's the number that the Prosecution gave me. I thought the OTP was well equipped for e-court. I thought I had a problem, but, you see, it's always their problem. When it comes to the use of e-court, they seem to have a problem. So let's just have a look at this one paragraph now which is marked, highlighted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about the indictment in the trial in Belgrade; that's right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's the current trial of the group accused for crimes in Zvornik, and I've already mentioned their names. I don't want to repeat them. They are names that appear in different witness testimony of the victims, and their nicknames. I'm sure you'll remember their nicknames. But I'm not interested in the trial, per se, as such, with respect to this document, but what the Prosecutor says in the indictment, and this is what he says in this paragraph: "The accused, Dusko Vuckovic, Dragan Slavkovic, Ivan Korac, Sinisa Filipovic, and Dragutin Dragicevic were volunteers who were included into a unit which was commanded by Witness Vojin Vuckovic, nicknamed Zuco, which unit was called Igor Markovic and the Yellow Wasps or "Zute Ose." According to written documentation which agrees on all points and is in conformity with the statement by Vojan Vuckovic, the witness interviewed, it emerges indubitably that this unit was within the composition of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik and that it did not represent a paramilitary formation outside the Command of the Staff of the Territorial Defence." Do you see this definition of the unit there, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you think that this unit, on the basis of what we can read here, has anything to do with the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Vuckovic brothers were from surrounding parts of Obrenovic, at Umka, and they could not have been in the Territorial Defence of Zvornik Municipality. That's a different state altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, that other state was recognised by the Western powers, but the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina never recognised it or didn't recognise it at the time; is that true? It is -- I'm not challenging that they went from Obrenovic to Zvornik, but this is what the Belgrade prosecutor says at the Belgrade trial; they became part of the Territorial Defence and established the Igor Markovic or "Zute Ose" unit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.
