Since an indictment relies on a number of documents that are in the hands of the prosecutor in Belgrade and it's on the basis of these documents that the prosecutor says this, I don't see how the witness can give an opinion, since he doesn't have the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has to do with relevance and probative value. As far as relevance is concerned, there is no problem whatsoever. The individuals whose names are mentioned in a number of testimonies, this has been confirmed by the witness on trial in Belgrade, so it is relevant since it relates to facts that were -- or things that were committed in Zvornik. As far as probative value is concerned, once the Bench has all the documents at hand, the Trial Chamber will assess the probative value of this. We have a document which stems from a legal entity, and all the people that were members of the Territorial Defence were connected to a paramilitary formation called the Yellow Wasps. This is what we can say so far. Please proceed, Mr. Seselj, and then we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document that I'd like to show here. Now, whether I'll have time, I don't know. It's one I received from the Prosecution. The number of it is 00741342. Can you bring it up on e-court? The document has three pages. I'd have to go through it, Judges, so do you want to take the break now or would it be better to do so straight away? It's an important document, and I'd like to go through it in its entirety, so when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The best would be to deal with this after the break, and the Registry, in the meantime, can call it up on the screen. It's two minutes past 12, and we shall resume in 20 minutes' time, and we will have an hour left after that, since we finish at quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Registrar has told me that you have one hour and 22 minutes left, which means that we will not finish today, unfortunately. Witness, you will have to come back tomorrow morning, unless Mr. Seselj finishes before his time. I don't know. Mr. Seselj, you have one hour and 22 minutes left. The Registrar has told me that the document you wish to display cannot be displayed, which explains why it's not on the screen. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this concerned is document, I must tell you that the Prosecution has received no information prior to Mr. Seselj's cross-examination, and I would like to object to this practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, normally speaking, as part of the cross-examination, the list of documents to be shown should be disclosed before the cross-examination. This should not happen halfway. I know you come up against a whole series of technical problems. Let us know about these problems and then we'll have a better understanding of this and why it is that you cannot meet this expectation, i.e., to provide the documents before the commencement of the cross-examination. I'll give you the floor back now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think you and your colleagues are conscious of the fact that just prior to the testimony of a Prosecution witness, I prepare myself for the cross-examination. That's all the possibility I have. I have been inundated by the Prosecution with vast quantities of documents, and I'm not complaining, but to look through them takes time. And I need to make a selection, of course, of those I can use. Now, the Prosecution sent me, as I said, heaps of material, heaps of documents, with no order in them, documents obtaining to all sorts of matters, so every time I have to leaf through many thousands of pages to find something that I can use with each individual witness. And you might have noticed that I seem a bit tired today because I just had two nights' sleep last night. I'm not complaining, but I don't expect the impossible of me. I don't have 15 associates like the Prosecution to do my work for me. If I had a secretary in the cell, then I could say such-and-such. Everything would be different then, but I haven't got that opportunity. Now, the warden won't let me employ a secretary, and my wife looked at me askance, too, when I happened to mention the possibility of this to her. So what can I do? I do the best that I can. Now, the fact that the Prosecutor is complaining, what can I do, how can I help him? He should have had all this in e-court. When I say the number, he should just press the button and it should pop up before him. So why are they not prepared for that. They announced the advent of e-court many years ago, so I can't help them in that regard, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this document put to the witness so we can go through the document together. It's an interesting one because it dates back to 1992. Ah, you don't even have it. You have to use my copy. Oh dear, oh dear. Very well. It's a document of the Serbian Security Service or rather the Republika Srpska, or, rather, the Security Services of Republika Srpska, signed by Dragoljub Andan, dating back to 1992. We'll see the date and the heading on page 1. It's the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Ministry of Interior, Centre of Security Services, Bijeljina, that's what it says at the top, and the date is the 20th of July, 1992. The title of the document is: "Information about the security situation in the territory of the Serb Municipality of Zvornik." And now I'd like to go through the document slowly and to hear the witness's views on each of the paragraphs. In paragraph 1, the situation on the fronts is explained, where the frontline towards Kalesija-Sapna is, and so on, and it says that there are actions on the part of a certain number of paramilitary formations which have still not been placed under the united command of the Army of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you seen that, Mr. Alic? It's the second part of the first paragraph. So that is the assessment made by the Serbian Security Service. And in the next paragraph, they go on to name the paramilitary units and say, according to available information that the service has, in the territory of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, three paramilitary units work in organised fashion; the unit under the command of a certain person called Zuca, the unit under the command of a certain man called Pivarski, and the unit under the command of a certain person called Niski. Have you heard of those three paramilitary units, as they call them, Mr. Alic? Did those names crop up in the witness and victims' testimony when they came from Zvornik to the territory under your control?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they did appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next paragraph, and this is what it says: "The most numerous and best-armed and organised is the unit under the command of the said person called Zuca. Allegedly, this is an individual who used to belong to the Serbian Radical Party or who belonged to the Serbian Radical Party, and because of inter-party conflicts, was excluded from the membership of the said party." Now, why is this important? This is a document which dates back to 1992, July 1992, in fact, where this observation is made, and we've had information so far that in 1991, he was excluded or, as he said, he's left the Serbian Radical Party, but the facts coincide. His unit numbers about 100 men who are armed with infantry weapons and dispose of a certain number of heavy machine-guns and three anti-aircraft guns built into the trucks. The unit is located at Caparde, where it has been accommodated in makeshift buildings. Of the total number of men, 80 of them come from the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, whereas the rest are from the territory of the Republic of Serbia, mostly persons prone to criminal actions." So here it says 80 from Zvornik and just 20 from Serbia. Let's continue. I don't know why my screen is being switched off and I lose the document. I have it now. I seemed to have pressed the wrong button. Anyway, it says: "In addition to Zuca, in the said unit, Rade Tanackovic is prominent." Turn over to the next page, please, the top of it. He's from Zvornik: " ... and Zuca's brother, nicknamed Repic, and" and then there's a mistake there, it says Repic, and then in brackets "This is a pathological case." So in 1992, they have described Repic as being a pathological case. The other two units have been accommodated in the outside area of Zvornik Municipality and come into town from time to time with infantry weapons, and they number about 20 people. Apart from criminal acts, such as the theft of cars, setting up their own check-points, stealing technical goods and furniture from houses left void, which they sell on the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like to know where the question lies. If the question is right at the end, it can only be a compound question. I would like to know when the question comes, because we are reading out an entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I think you're laying -- please lay the foundations to your questions. I assume there's going to be a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to have a foundation for each and every question. Without those papers, I cannot do anything. I don't know what was happening. I used these as sort of landmarks. And the Prosecutor is really impatient. He interrupted me at the very moment when I was about to ask my question, and we waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you know these things that are listed here in this document; that the Serbian Security Service, at the Bijeljina centre, had problems with three paramilitary units that are described in this manner?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that. This is the first time that I see this document, and this is the first time I hear about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And have you heard that the members of the Yellow Wasps were arrested in the course of July in Zvornik and were taken to prison in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let us move on. Those units, in particular the one that is commanded by Zuca, intensified its activities aimed at the legal authorities in the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. And I don't want to read the whole paragraph, prompting the Prosecutor to jump to his feet. Let me now ask a question. Do you know that they mistreated Serb civilian authorities in Zvornik after the majority of Muslims had already moved out of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that this was also said at the Belgrade trial, that they would walk into the sessions of the Zvornik Presidency with machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know details, but I do know that the official authorities there have problems with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that at one point, they caught Branko Grujic, the first accused in the Belgrade trial, tied him up, and paraded him around?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the Muslim side would have laughed heartily had you heard that, wouldn't you? But at any rate, the document goes on to say the service has information about Zuca's intentions to use armed force and violence to influence the authorities, to effect certain changes in the personnel policies, so that Zuca's people would be appointed to appropriate functions and posts in the municipality. One of the aspects of the pressure is taking control over the check-points in the town, and earlier cases of arrest of a certain number of members of the government in May of this year. In addition to the above, members of this formation ensure that they could legalize their criminal activities." Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that a huge mass of Serb refugees from Tuzla simply overflowed Zvornik after the armed conflict, or the attack, as you term it, after the Muslims left or withdrew from Zvornik? Do you know that there was a huge influx of Serb refugees from Tuzla to this area?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that they moved into Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know, on the other hand, that various gangs in Zvornik were trying to loot those very houses before the arrival of the refugees and before the refugees move in?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that they drove a lot of the white goods, refrigerators, ovens, even construction material, across the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the JNA -- do you know when the JNA column was attacked in Tuzla; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The 15th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: About 200 JNA soldiers were killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figure because I was not in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this murder of over 200 soldiers, JNA soldiers in Tuzla, and the huge influx of Serb refugees from Tuzla, could it have intensified the anti-Muslim animosity amongst Serbs in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it could have done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that hatred feeds on itself?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Something happens on the Serb side, the Muslims' hatred increases, and then something happens on the Muslim side and then the Serbs' hatred increases, and it's a vicious circle with no end?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Okay, let us move on. Through its operational work, the service has obtained unverified information, as it is indicated here, that Zuco has contacted members of the Green Berets from Kalesija in order to hand over -- surrender the frontline at Caparde, thereby cutting off the only communication route with Romanija and to create an unimpeded -- to create conditions for the Serbian municipality of Zvornik to be taken over?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether Mr. Seselj is quoting something or whether these are his own words, when he talks about these services and what relates to operations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am moving through the document. I indicated that, and the witness understands that's what I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that right, Mr. Alic? Well, you understand everything and the Prosecutor doesn't understand a thing. Well, the last sentence in this paragraph, and then I'm going to ask you the question. For this concession, foreign currency was offered to the amount of 350.000 German marks on the side -- on the part of the Green Berets, while Zuca requested 500.000 German marks. Are you aware of this kind of talks between the Green Berets and Zuca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, this is the first I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, Zuco will be thankful to you denying this, denying that you know of this. I don't know whether this actually happened or not, and the service itself indicates that this is unverified information, but I wanted to hear your opinion because it is quite important. Then I move on. For an overall insight into this paramilitary unit and its possible influence on the very unfavorable development of the security situation in this area, it is important to bear in mind the connection between Zuco and Vidovic, Milje [phoen], killed on the 17th of July, 1992, in Mali Zvornik in unclear circumstances." Do you know about this man, Milje Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say in the text: " ... and we had operational intelligence that he was supposed to get in touch with the former JNA officer, Sasha Sedinovc [phoen], who in his statement," turn over to the next page: "Through the organs of the Serb army admitted that earlier this year he had been hired by the Dutch police and that it was his task to get in touch with this man, Vidovic, who allegedly has some codes and some instructions for further work. It is also interesting to note that when Vidovic was killed, a Dictaphone was found -- a tape-recorder was found in his apartment with a tape containing the recording from the meeting of the Staff of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Army, BiH, in Zvornik." Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that various foreign intelligence services were operating in that area? Did you have them on your side of the frontline?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is and if you had them, then there had to be some operating on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And would it be possible, if it were in their interests, for them to stoke the flames between Serbs and Muslims if it were in their interests to have the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina to escalate?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what their intentions were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us see what the conclusions were in this document. It transpires from everything that was transpired above that Zuco is carrying out his criminal activities for larger sums of money, with the assistance of some members of the government of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection. The witness is asked to speculate. He answered that he didn't know the intent, but the question was not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Seselj is asking you whether you knew whether the security services, be it of Bosnia-Herzegovina or of Serbia, had ties with foreign services, and you said, "Yes." So I thought I understood that your answer dealt with the two sides. So when you answered, "Yes," to this question, is this speculation or do you have specific information on this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Mr. President, specify, I did not say that those foreign intelligence services were cooperating either with the Muslim or the Serb intelligence services. I said they were just operating in the area. I didn't say that they were cooperating with anyone. And the witness confirmed that the operation of those services was felt on the Muslim side. We didn't go into detail because I didn't -- I don't know the details myself. I don't want to confuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Without talking about cooperation, to your knowledge, did foreign intelligence services operate in this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the answer is "yes." They were operating in many ways through humanitarian organisations, various representative offices, but I do think they were operating there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me finish this document, with your permission, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Everything that is presented above indicates that Zuco performs his criminal activities exclusively for large sums of money, with the assistance of some members of the government of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik," and now this is my comment: So he has assistance from these people, through whom he's trying to conceal his activities: "In this relation, it is to be expected that he might, in light of his pretensions and aspirations, to carry out armed pressure on the government in order to achieve a full takeover. It is our assessment that the current activity of those paramilitary units might lead to huge consequences for the security of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik, and in this -- for the purpose of preventing this and to making it impossible, we propose that a special unit of the Republika Srpska -- of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP be sent there in the area of Zvornik." So do you know whether, after this date, and I forgot the date - it's on page 1 - that there was a large-scale intervention by the special police of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as it was styled then, and that members of these paramilitary formations were actually all arrested; you know that? You were there. You were in range, in Sapna.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But did you not observe some large-scale movements of special units at that time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I was not concerned with those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, if you don't know that, I can't now force you into making a statement. Now I am about to spring a surprise on you, on the Prosecution -- well, rather, it is not a surprise for the Prosecution and for the Trial Chamber because they've already received it during the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the surprise, there are two things I'd like to know, in terms of this document which comes from the Prosecution, because it's the Prosecution that disclosed it to the Defence. There are two important items here. First, I note here that in this document, can comes from the Republika Srpska, Bijeljina, July 20, 1992, people from Zuce, representing a group of 100 people, of which 80 come from Zvornik and 20 from Serbia. So there's a majority of locals. Since you interviewed Zuco, who is Repic's brother, could you tell us whether he addressed this with you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you missed a piece of information. This unit, Ivo Markovic, the Yellow Wasps, was set up in Zuce, became its commander on the 27th of April after Kuljagrad [phoen] fell. This is when the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and the special unit of Zene [phoen] from Pancevo and Arkan's units a withdrew from Zvornik. That was when this unit was set up and that's when Zuco was appointed commander. Up until that time, he did not have any command responsibility there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has just given evidence, and I object to this. However, in the very clever way Mr. Seselj read verbatim, the so-called testimony of a person, without calling this person, without respecting any of the rules, 92 ter, 92 bis, or anything, and I object to this kind of a practice. The OTP is not able to cross-examine this person and to assess the relevance and the reliability of what is mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your objection is now noted on the transcript. The second thing, sir: This Zuco, according to this document, it seems that Zuco is undergoing criminal activities, motivated mainly by greed and nothing else, nothing that would have to do with politics, and the best proof that we have in this document is the paragraph where he in contact with the Green Berets. So unless I'm wrong, the Green Berets were an organisation that was internal to Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was a group of people who wanted to fight for Bosnia-Herzegovina. Weren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore, this Zuco is in contact with the Green Berets, with the Muslim side, and it seems that he had contacts for many reasons. There seems to be no politics involved here. What do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first that I hear about this possibility, and I can't really comment on it. There's no need for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time that you hear this? Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to respond to the objection made by the Prosecution. The document that we went through with the witness is not a statement. It is an official police document from the Centre of Security Services in Bijeljina, signed by the chief of the Security Services Centre, Dragan Andan. Dragan Andan is not a witness that I intend to call. I might put him on the list if I need him. But this is an official document disclosed to me by the Prosecution God knows when - several years ago - but it bears the number that was assigned to it by the Prosecution. It is their exhibit, as they call it. It's not mine. I am using it in the cross-examination legitimately. How can I use it, if not in the cross-examination? It's the only way in which I can do it. I cannot just put it in the mail and send it to you. I have to find a witness through which I can deal with it, because I myself don't know whether all this is true. I just know that it is written in this document, and I don't know if it's true or not. The only thing I know, is that this sentence that in 1991, Zuco was a member, and that sometime in September or October, he was no longer a member, it was his version of events that he left, and our version of events is that he was expelled. And I don't know the details, because he was not a major figure in our ranks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What you have just said is now on the transcript. However, when I said that it was a document from -- that came from the Prosecution, I think I said "everything." One last item, Witness. At the very beginning of this text, in the first paragraph -- this is a document that you do not know, but since you were there, maybe you could shed some light on this. This document seems to say that these paramilitary formations are -- there are three of them, and that these three paramilitary formations are not under the command of Republika Srpska. This is written, black on white, here in this document from the very onset, and this might have consequences for us, for the Bench. You were involved. You were on the ground. You were there. You had an official post in the War Presidency, and you had functions in the different police stations. So according to you, these kind of paramilitary formations, and here three are mentioned -- let's talk about the Yellow Wasps, for example. According to you, were these people alongside and autonomous or were they under command, the Command of the Army of Republika Srpska? What is your opinion on this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't say with any precision. All I can do is to speak about the period until the 8th of April, 1992, and everything happened after the 8th of April, 1992, all that, when we were expelled from Zvornik and when we were outside those events. So what went on in the town of Zvornik, I really can't testify about that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have the surprise now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to draw your attention, Mr. President, and it's something the Prosecution knows about, and it is this: That this unit was formed as the territorial Defence unit of Zvornik on the 27th of April, and that's not in dispute. That was found to be so during the indictment in Belgrade and so on. But it was set up as a Territorial Defence unit, but it went off on its own afterwards and there was no stronger force until the special police forces arrived to overcome it as being a renegade. Now, the surprise: I received a statement from Vojin Vuckovic today, nicknamed Zuca. I have provided photocopies for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. The Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, once again. The accused is testifying on all this, once again, in a repetitive fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we've taken due note of this. But this Vojin, Mr. Seselj, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be placed on the overhead projector so that Mr. Alic can follow. This is a statement that has been authenticated or certified in the 4th District Court in Belgrade yesterday. I was faxed it this morning. The date is the 20th of May up there at the top, and he first of all provides all his personal data and says that watching your testimony last week, he was astounded by the lies. Those were his words. Don't consider yourselves -- don't think this comes from me. I had some observations to make with respect to false testimony, but you did tell some truth as well. Anyway, he says he felt the need to present the facts about events that he took part in personally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, please. Can we please look at what has been authenticated, certified, according to you? Is it the signature, the statement? You know that I was having problems with this, so please be very accurate, and the transcript needs to be accurate. It seems that it's only the signature once again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Madam Judge, on page 4 you have the certification, and on page 3 you have the signature and the stamp. Actually, they were two pieces of paper, because obviously on page 4 is the certification. You have the photocopy of that here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have a PhD in Law. Could you tell me whether, in your legal system -- I'm not asking you to testify, but to answer a legal question. You are both counsel and accused here, since you are self-represented. If you had counsel, I would ask the question to your counsel. You have no counsel, so I'll put the question to you. In your own legal system, somebody is making a statement either in typewritten form or handwritten form, and signs, if this certificate is false, is there -- is it an offence in your -- is it an offence according to your legal system, that you could be charged -- that this person could be charged with --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and criminal proceedings can be taken against me if there's a false authentication, false certification. And your service will be able to check this out in the 4th District Court in Belgrade during the afternoon. The Prosecutor could have actually done that during the second break if he was provided with this document in the first break. The OTP could have checked this out and could have been sent the same document. Now, as far as the certification is concerned, only the signature is certified, not the truthfulness of what is stated. The clerk of the court has authenticated the fact that it is Vojin Vuckovic who signed it, but he's not authenticating the truth. Who knows where the truth lies? But I am in search of the truth, and I'm more successful along that path than the Prosecutor is, as you've been able to convince yourselves of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, just for clarification, does this authentication require Mr. Vuckovic to be present in the court before the authentication was given?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, each individual who provides me with a statement agrees that he will be a Defence witness, and in the last sentence on page 3, Vojin Vuckovic states as follows: "I give this statement voluntarily and at my own request, and agree that Professor, Dr. Vojislav Seselj can use it before The Hague Tribunal. I should like to emphasize that I am ready to appear in The Hague exclusively as a Defence witness called by Professor Dr. Vojislav Seselj." Whereas the Prosecutor was not going to call him as a Prosecution witness, so I don't suppose you're going to seize him from me, are you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you're not answering my fellow Judge's question. He asked you whether, in your legal system, the person asking for authentication of a document and a signature must be present when, in court, a stamp is set on the document, that is recorded, the person -- must the person be present when this person is asking for a stamp to be affixed on the document? By definition, the agent who's going to stamp the document is supposed to check that the person in front of him has exactly the same signature as the one that is on the document. This is the question you were asked. Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he must be present, absolutely so. Otherwise, a clerk, certifying somebody's signature without his presence and without the identification card of the person signing, would be in prison. Not only does he certify the signature, but the person has to sign in front of the court official. He can't bring in a signed copy, but he has to sign in front of the court clerk, and there must be two or three copies, which some are stored in the archives, and everybody can check whether that is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking, Mr. Seselj, is that in both documents that you have put to us, the authentication has been provided on a separate sheet of paper. It would have been natural to put the authentication directly on the page where the signature occurred.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Harhoff, look, this statement covered two pages, quite obviously, and so what is authenticated is the last page of the second -- the last page of the statement, the second page. But when you send it by fax, as they are actually four pages on two pieces of paper, then we receive four pages. I think that's clear, but the Prosecution can check that out in Belgrade. They can send a fax telling them what it was that Vojin Vuckovic signed and had authenticated at the 4th District Court in Belgrade yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's exactly what my problem is, but the OTP cannot check as quickly as Mr. Seselj says we could. And even so, this does not explain why this certification -- why this stamp is not affixed right next to the signature of Vuckovic. The third page is blank, for the most part, and the certification could very well have been affixed there. So I still have questions pending regarding this. Secondly, I'd like to know under which Rule Mr. Seselj would like to use this statement with, 92 bis, 92 ter, 92 quater? Does he want to read it extensively, like he did with the previous document? And I believe that if, once again, we have a full reading of the entire statement, I would like to add that the OTP cannot cross-examine this witness, and therefore this witness should be called during the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This is noted on the transcript now. We have ten minutes left. Please continue, Mr. Seselj, and finish.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not my intention to offer you up any document under 92 bis, ter, quater, or whatever, because I'm categorically opposed to the application of those Rules in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence in this trial. I'm absolutely against that, so if I'm against something, I can't allow myself to do something that I do not allow the Prosecutor to do. But since this is rather lengthy, I'd like to go back to a document that was photocopied during the break. This will last ten minutes, and then tomorrow we can go back, in the time we have, to Vojin Vuckovic's statement, and given enough time for the Prosecutor to check this out in Belgrade to see if it's authentic or not, if you agree, because we're not going to get through everything and I don't want to leave this document up in the air because I have quite a few questions relating to it. May I now have the document of the Centre for Research into the Crimes Against the Serbian Population, sent by Vojan Ivanisevic [phoen], and you can see that on page 1, and the attached documents sent to my Defence team and it has to do with Asim Alic and the information that they have on Asim Alic from Zvornik. So we can move on to page 2, and in paragraph 1 there, it says the following -- is it on the overhead projector? This is the information that they have on you, Mr. Alic, so you can give me your views and tell me whether it's correct or not: "He came to Zvornik from Belgrade in 1991, and he was appointed assistant commander of the police station straight away. According to many indications, he had links in Belgrade with the representatives of the Party of Democratic Action, who, just like Naser Oric, and not only the two of them, persuaded him to go to Bosnia and place himself at the disposal of the Muslim leadership. In Zvornik and the surrounding villages, he trained members of the Green Berets or, rather, the Patriotic League. In that work, he closely cooperated with Alan Karlovic [phoen] from Bratunac," and in brackets it says "I'd like to remind you that the Muslims through the SDA sent their young men for training in Croatia in their masses. The instruction for sending candidates to the training center, the MUP of the Republic of Croatia with the signature of Hasan Cengic we have already sent to your team. He was known for his fundamental -- extreme fundamentalism and hostility towards his colleagues who were Serbs." Is that right, Mr. Alic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM ALIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Thanks for that brief answer, just a yes or no. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. To the extent that excerpts are read verbatim, I believe that it would also be good to read the cover page of this document, because it explains how Mr. Seselj obtained this document, and it explains the relationship between the author of this document and Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, for each and everyone to understand this document and to know exactly what probative value is to be granted to this document, I assume that this document was sent to you at your request. Could you tell us exactly how you obtained this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I obtained this document at the request of my legal advisers. I can read it out. I hope that you won't deduct it from my time, because this is something at the Prosecution request. But it says in the attached letter: "We enclose documents, the documents that you requested about the Muslim policeman Asim Alic from Zvornik." So we did request it: "In our documents, the named person was recorded as one of the people responsible for the persecution and suffering of Serbs in that municipality. The documents of our institution is at your disposal for any matters related to assisting the Defence of respected Dr. Vojislav Seselj. We wish you every success in this responsible and humane task." That is what Milivoj Ivanisevic says, who is the head of the centre for research into crimes committed against the Serb nation, and he is somebody who has published seven or eight books on that same topic, and some of those books are ones that I'm going to use here in court with other witnesses. So obviously he is well disposed towards my Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I must absolutely repeat what I have said on many occasions about these statements. The issue of its probative value cannot be raised if the accused is not asking for this document to be tendered into evidence. If the accused eventually asks for the document to be tendered into evidence, then we must now solve, either now or when he will ask for this document to be tendered, we must solve the problem of the reliability of this document. But I really do not see how any probative value can be granted to this document if it's not tendered. The only thing I will keep in mind are the answers given by the witness in connection to questions that were put according to this document, but this document has no value by itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In line of what has just been said, I've already told you this, you are showing documents, presenting documents, and not asking for these documents to be tendered. And as my fellow Judge just said excellently, the Trial Chamber cannot take them into account, for -- the Trial Chamber can only use the witness's answer on the transcript to check the probative value of whatever, which is why I have asked you on a number of occasions to make sure that the important documents to your case are translated. And once they are shown to the witness, they must be translated, and then you must ask for these documents to be tendered. And once these documents are admitted, then these documents may benefit from probative value. I've said this over and over again. It seems that you have another vision of things or another view on things. And my fellow Judges want to safeguard the rights of the Defence, you know, and we've alerted you on this issue on many occasions. You might have very interesting documents, very important documents, but if you do not tender them and they are not admitted, the Chamber will not even look at them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you remember full well that I collected together 160 documents, along with the wholehearted assistance of Slavko Aleksic [phoen], and Vasil Vasilevic [phoen], Vranislav Graviljevic Brne [phoen] whose alleged, and I insist on this word, alleged crimes are ascribed to me, and from which we can see they weren't volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party at all at that time. Now, I put those documents to Mr. Theunens, the military expert, when you categorically refused to admit them into evidence. Now, after that, I'm not tendering any more documents. I haven't done so. And why? Because it is up to me to challenge the Prosecution witness through my cross-examination, and in order to challenge him, I use various documents. Now, you can treat his answers to my questions in any way you want. I think that I have been successful in overthrowing this witness's testimony, at least in the part which relates to the indictment raised against me. Now, how you're going to treat this later on is up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we are going to finish now. I understand your position. You've told us already. Once, the Trial Chamber did not admit some documents. I was against this, because I felt that these were reliable and that the probative value could be assessed afterwards. This was ruled by the Trial Chamber. But other documents can be shown, and so long as they remain reliable and relevant, then there might be grounds for admitting these. My colleagues and I might refuse to admit them, but it's not because we took this stance once that this will be the case forever. So if a document is reliable, if a document is relevant, then it may have a probative value, and in that case there's no reason to dismiss it. Let me finish. This last document, which seems to stem from an association or organisation which should list those crimes committed against the Serbs, I believe that this organisation is very similar to the one headed by Mrs. Natasha Kandic. If this body has conducted work, if this is a recognised body, then there is certainly a modicum of reliability. There would be no reason, then, to dismiss this document. This is what I wish to tell you. It's not because in a particular case some documents were rejected, that this is applied at all times. Let me also draw your attention to the fact that you are putting arguments forward which may carry some weight in your Defence, but these documents need to be part of the proceedings, unfortunately. Otherwise, we will not be able to do anything about them. It is now time to stop, because it is a quarter past 1.00. I would ask the Registrar to tell me tomorrow morning how much time you have left. Normally speaking, we should finish this witness's testimony. Witness, I am sorry, but in light of all the procedural issues that have been raised, you are still here today, and you will be asked to come back tomorrow morning at 8.30. But then it will be finished, because we have another witness after you. Is this a problem for you? Can you come tomorrow morning?
